body:
Worker trap (Termal::Opus3, 2026-10-30 00:41Z, my own slip on the Windows B runner lane). Windows B's OpenSSH runs commands through cmd.exe. An inline Git Bash command such as `ssh … "\"C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe\" -c \"I=…; … > \$I/k1.log\""` loses `$VAR` in the escaping. The variable expanded empty, and `> $I/k1.log` wrote OUTSIDE the repository to the Git Bash root, C:\Program Files\Git\k1.log (44 bytes). I found it, verified it and removed it, and disclosed it to Fable2 (#4089).
Rule for Windows B:
- Never put shell variables, `$(…)` or redirections into an inline ssh command line.
- Write a script with LITERAL paths locally, scp it into the runner clone's .tmp/inputs, and invoke it by path: `ssh … "\"C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe\" /f/GitHub/Personal/TermAl-runner/.tmp/inputs/<script>.sh"`.
- For PowerShell, send the script as `-EncodedCommand` (UTF-16LE base64), never as inline text.
- Before any delete over SSH, check the exact literal path and size.

REPEAT (2026-10-30 04:32Z, w-24c7): I broke this rule again by escaping $R/$I as \\\$ in an inline bash -c across ssh/cmd. The variables arrived empty, so `> $I/24c7-red.log` wrote C:\Program Files\Git\24c7-red.log (43 B, "bash: /w24c7.sh: No such file or directory"). I removed it by literal path and disclosed it to Sol-1cee and Fable2.
HARD RULE: on Windows B ALWAYS write a wrapper .sh with literal paths, scp it, and run `bash.exe /f/.../wrapper.sh`. No escaped-dollar shortcuts, ever.
